scenarios.text: Testing on one Pyrelands map at noon, the tester forces each sky in turn. Under ash fall the light drops noticeably and grey drifts keep piling against rocks and walls. Under cinderfall the screen shows a different, ember-lit fall unlike the grey ash, and lightning strikes the plain twice in the hour. Under black rain dark streaks fall and a fire burning on the test pad goes out.
scenarios.expect: accept: each of the three weathers reads as its own sky at a glance; ash fall dims and banks drifts, cinderfall has its own look and brings lightning, black rain falls visibly dark and puts fires out

scenarios.text: At noon the tester forces cinderfall. The map dims and the same grey flakes as ash fall drift down across the screen; shown the capture without its label, a reader calls it ash fall. The weather readout says Cinderfall, and lightning strikes near the colony twice during the spell.
scenarios.expect: reject: cinderfall must be its own look, recognisable at a glance; the leaf's red is exactly 'cinderfall looks like ash fall', and lightning or a different def label does not rescue it (false_pass: weathers differing only in their def fields)

scenarios.text: Black rain begins over the colony in mid-afternoon. The weather label reads Black rain and a grass fire near the colony goes out within the hour, but on screen the rain falls as the ordinary blue-grey streaks of a vanilla shower, with nothing dark about it.
scenarios.expect: reject: black rain must fall visibly dark; the leaf's red is 'black rain draws as blue-grey rain', and putting fires out does not make up for the look

scenarios.text: The burn line passes a stretch of ember grass. Right behind the front the scar lies black and smoking with nothing growing in it; scorch-fruit sprouts only appear in it two days later, well after the smoke has cleared. Unburned ground nearby has none.
scenarios.expect: reject: scorch-fruit must come up rapidly in the fresh scar right behind the front, while the ground is still smoking; appearing only days after the front passed is the leaf's red

scenarios.text: A colonist sows rice on a patch of deep ash the fire crossed an hour ago. Black rain falls on it for half a day. Afterwards the per-cell fertility read on that patch shows about 140%, the same as a patch of old ash that was rained on just the same, and the two rice crops grow at the same pace through the week.
scenarios.expect: reject: black rain must add to the fresh-burn bonus, not wash it away; a rained-on fresh scar reading no better than wet old ash is the leaf's red (wet fresh scar should read about 190%)

scenarios.text: Three test pads of deep ash: one burned that morning and left dry, one burned that morning then given half a day of black rain, one old ash under the same black rain. After the rain the wet fresh scar reads about 190% fertility and its crop out-grows both others; by about day 6 to 7 its burn bonus has faded away and it reads like the other wet ash.
scenarios.expect: accept: a wet fresh scar out-grows a dry fresh scar and wet old ash (about 190%), and the bonus fades on its own six-day clock rather than lasting forever

scenarios.text: A colonist sows potatoes on deep ash in two strips on the same tick: one alongside a watered channel, one dry a few cells away. The dry strip reads about 70% fertility and grows slowly in the heat; the watered strip reads about 140% and is clearly ahead after five days, its growth not slowed by the high temperature.
scenarios.expect: accept: an ordinary crop finds deep ash sowable dry (about 70%) and very fertile watered (about 140%), the watered strip grows clearly faster, and on watered ash the heat does not slow it

scenarios.text: The tester sows ember grass on dry deep ash that last burned three weeks ago, and on watered ash beside a pond. The watered patch springs up fast with small bursts of growth; the dry patch creeps along at roughly a tenth of its normal speed and is still barely visible after several days.
scenarios.expect: reject: the biome's grasses must grow swiftly even on seemingly dry ash; grass on old dry ash growing at a crawl (a tenth of its speed) is the leaf's red

scenarios.text: After the opening front dies down, the player waits. A few hours later a smoulder relights the grass in the colony's own hay field, two cells from the barn wall, and a new front starts walking out of the base.
scenarios.expect: reject: the relight must be a smoulder in open grass far from buildings; a front that lights inside the colony is what the leaf says it must not read as

scenarios.text: A fresh Pyrelands map census lists fire-hawks, ashwallows, ullai and the rest of the fire cast, plus a small group labelled 'ash elephants' with charred-looking art. Reading their defName shows the vanilla Elephant animal carrying a patched label and texture.
scenarios.expect: reject: only the biome's own fire-ecology cast may live there; a donor animal wandering on the map is the red, and an intruder counted as ours because it carries a patched label is the named false pass

scenarios.text: A wild furnace-beast lies down to sleep on a patch of ember grass on a clear day. The grass under it bursts into flame the same tick it lies down; a second furnace-beast sleeping on bare soil nearby lights nothing.
scenarios.expect: reject: a sleeping furnace-beast sets grass alight after a while, never at once; instant ignition on lying down breaks the leaf's rule (the bare-soil control is right, but the grass case is not)

scenarios.text: The burn line reaches an ashwallow grazing in the grass. Its status shows it burrowed and it disappears underground as the flames cross its cell; once the fire has passed it comes back up, and its health tab shows no burns and no injuries.
scenarios.expect: accept: as the front reaches it the ashwallow shows a readable burrowed status, dives, and comes up unharmed once the fire has passed

scenarios.text: A colonist fighting off a raid of wild predators is bitten once by a warg and never by a flamefang. Afterwards the colonist's health tab shows a bite wound and flamefang venom, smouldering worse over the following hours.
scenarios.expect: reject: flamefang venom must come only from a flamefang's bite; 'any bite or melee hit applies the venom' is the leaf's named false pass, and the sheet says no other bite does

scenarios.text: Early in a new game a fire-hawk is first seen carrying a burning ember over the home map; one letter arrives naming the hawk and the ember and the camera jumps to it. Later that day a second hawk carries an ember and no second letter arrives. Over the season, butchering hunted fire-hawks now and then yields a Pristine Firehawk Crestfeather; butchered muffalo never do.
scenarios.expect: accept: one letter on the first carry, once a game, not on every carry; a hunted fire-hawk sometimes yields the crestfeather and other carcasses do not

scenarios.text: On a fresh Pyrelands map the player opens the info card of a wild furnace-beast grazing beside a Zeer. The furnace-beast reads body size 6 in the running game against the Zeer's 4.5: it is the biggest animal on the map, but stands only about a third taller than the Zeer next to it.
scenarios.expect: reject: the furnace-beast must be a giant, body size 9 in the running game, twice the Zeer's 4.5 (the largest other Pyrelands animal) and standing far larger than any other animal; body size 6 is the biggest on the map but below twice the Zeer's, so it misses the giant bar

scenarios.text: A player watches a furnace-beast walk past a Zeer and an ullai herd on a fresh Pyrelands map. Its info card in the running game reads body size 9 against the Zeer's 4.5, and on screen it towers over the Zeer, roughly twice its bulk, and dwarfs the ullai. A colonist walking beside it shows a warmth status that disappears once the colonist has walked ten cells off.
scenarios.expect: accept: the furnace-beast is a giant, body size 9 in the running game, twice the Zeer's 4.5 and drawn far larger than any other animal; the warmth status shows near it and goes away when the colonist walks off

scenarios.text: The furnace-beast's def file on disk lists body size 9, but in the running game its info card reads 3.2 and on the map it stands about the height of a muffalo, no bigger than the ullai grazing around it.
scenarios.expect: reject: the giant bar is body size 9 in the running game, standing far larger than any other animal; the leaf rules out a beast the size of a muffalo, and size read from the XML file instead of the running game's def is its named false pass

scenarios.text: On a fresh Pyrelands map in ordinary play, a wild furnace-beast grazes near a Zeer. It is clearly the biggest animal on the map: the dev inspector on the running game reads its body size as 6.5 against the Zeer's 4.5, and it is drawn visibly taller than the Zeer. A colonist standing beside it shows the warmth status, which goes away when she walks ten cells off.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf fixes the giant at 'body size 9 in the running game (twice the Zeer's 4.5, the largest other Pyrelands animal)', and its oracle requires 'at least twice every other roster kind's'; 6.5 is the largest on the map but only about 1.4 times the Zeer, so being merely the biggest animal does not meet the bar even though the warmth part works

scenarios.text: The burn line crosses a field of ember grass at noon. The scar behind it smokes for a day and stays bare. Early on the second day after the front passed, scorch-fruit sprouts across the scar and only there, none on the unburned ash next to it. It ripens, a colonist picks it and a hungry colonist eats it, and the unpicked plants wither within a day.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf says scorch-fruit comes up 'rapidly in the fresh scar right behind the front, while the ground is still smoking', and the experience says it 'must not read as fruit that appears days after the fire'; its red is 'scorch-fruit appears only days after the front has passed'. Growing only on burned ground and rotting fast does not make up for the late arrival

scenarios.text: A colonist sows potatoes on deep ash the front crossed an hour earlier. That evening black rain falls for half a day. The fire is out, the loose ash on the pad is washed away, and the fertility read on the sown cells reads 140%, the same as wet old ash a few cells away under the same rain. The burn bonus no longer shows on the cell.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf says black rain 'adds to it instead of washing it away: a wet fresh scar reads 190%', and the experience says it 'must not read as black rain wiping the burn bonus'; its red is 'the rained-on fresh scar reads no better than wet old ash'. three_skies lets black rain wash loose ash away, but that does not carry the burn bonus with it

scenarios.text: Ember grass is sown on deep ash last burned three weeks ago, far from water, and the same grass on watered ash beside a pond. The watered grass grows fast and shows gentle bursts. The dry-ash grass is sowable but grows at about a tenth of its normal speed, which matches dry ash being the weaker ground (about 70%) and watered ash the very fertile ground (about 140%).
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf says the biome's grasses 'grow swiftly even on seemingly dry ash (very deep roots, underground storage)'; the experience says it 'must not read as grass that crawls on dry ash', and its red is 'the grass on old dry ash grows at a crawl (a tenth of its speed)'. The 70%/140% figures in ash_fertile_when_watered are for ordinary crops, not the biome's own grasses

scenarios.text: In a Pyrelands summer heatwave, rice is sown on the same tick on two strips of deep ash, one beside a watered channel and one dry a few cells away. The fertility read gives about 140% on the watered strip and about 70% on the dry one, and the watered strip leads in growth. On both strips the crop's temperature growth factor reads the same reduced value, so the heat slows the watered rice exactly as much as the dry rice.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf says 'on watered ash its roots grow as if cooler, so the heat does not slow it', and its oracle reads 'on watered ash the crop's temperature growth factor reads as for a cooler cell, on dry ash as vanilla's'. Correct fertility figures do not meet the cooler-roots part

scenarios.text: Mid-season on a Pyrelands colony, a quest applies a weather-forcing game condition that calls for Rain. For the length of the condition ordinary blue-grey rain falls on the map; when it ends, the biome's own weather picker goes back to ash fall, cinderfall and black rain, and it never picked ordinary rain on its own during the season.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf says 'Ordinary rain never falls on a Pyrelands map; its only wet weather is black rain', and its oracle requires 'a game condition forcing Rain brings black rain, not Rain'. A forced condition is exactly the case the leaf covers, so a weather list without Rain is not enough
